blocks.text: Share the Moment
When a kid earns 3 stars on a song, they can send the recording to Mom, and Mom can send something back. A first-time flow for kids aged 6–9 on iPad, and for their parent on the phone.

The goal from the brief: strengthen the kid's own sense of accomplishment, and turn it into a positive, empowering moment with their parents. The kid only decides whether to share, never with whom: the recording goes to the parent set up on the kid's profile.
Who it's for
Kids aged 6–9 play for different reasons, and each changes what sharing means to them.

Wants to learn: sharing is proof of mastery, "I can really play this now".
Parents said so: practice becomes pride, and Mom's reply replaces "did you practice?".
It's a game: the send animation and the reply reveal feel like a reward round.
Design rules

Voice-over on every prompt. Text is a backup, never the only cue.
People are avatars, not names. "Mom" is her avatar in the app.
One obvious action per screen, with large touch targets and no typing.
Every tap gets sound and motion feedback.
No negative signals for the kid: no "not opened yet", no "0 listens".
The kid always chooses to send. Nothing is shared automatically.
The flow
Kid flow

You did it! (glow-up) → the stickers scatter → You are a star! with three stars → Share the moment → the song flies to Mom → Shared. Later, Mom's reply arrives as a notification and opens as a message with her sticker.
Parent flow
An SMS → the listen page with the kid's recording and the effort story → a short message and a sticker → Sent.
Each step is designed in layers: what's on screen, what the kid hears, what moves, and what they can do. Sound carries the meaning, so reading is never required.
What the 3 stars mean

Every note: every note played, no wrong or missed keys.
On the beat: each note played on time.
Both hands: played hands-together, not one hand at a time.
A missing star tells the kid exactly what to work on next. Mom sees the same three, so she can praise something specific.
Metrics

Sharing: shares ÷ 3-star results, first-time vs. habitual sharers.
Parent engagement: link open rate, listen-through, reply rate, time to reply.
Stickiness: the kid comes back within 24 hours of a reply.
Retention: 7- and 30-day retention, sharers vs. non-sharers.
Next steps

Confirm the thresholds behind the prompt's sub-states.
Multiple receivers: both parents, grandparents, separate households.
Sticker book: a sticker for every completed song, and maybe Mom's reply stickers too.
